A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Proact-VL and Live Gaming Dataset research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, training and inference ablations, judge-robustness analyses and a human user study.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds Video-MME, LongVideoBench and human-alignment evaluations.

M1.justification: The one-second streaming procedure, FLAG-token response head, transition-weighted classification and stability losses, and dual-cache reverse-RoPE inference remain unchanged. Implementation details promoted into Section 5.1 already appeared in v1 Appendix C.3.

E1.justification: v3 Appendix I expands general video evaluation beyond the existing MVBench experiment by adding Video-MME and LongVideoBench. This adds subtitle-assisted video question answering and long-context video reasoning coverage; the original gaming, Ego4D and streaming evaluations remain.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator membership, including Qwen3-VL on MVBench and the original gaming baselines. The added benchmarks and human-alignment study reuse previously evaluated models, including Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, LiveCC-7B-Base and LiveStar.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce substantial new protocol content: eight uniformly sampled frames with and without subtitles on Video-MME, eight-frame evaluation across LongVideoBench duration groups, and human scoring of 300 outputs from 100 instances. The human analysis adds a 1–9 scoring rubric, tie-excluded preference agreement and calibration metrics. Existing training settings, splits and response thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix L directly tests whether LiveU and FinalQ agree with human judgments, examining both pairwise preferences and method-specific score calibration. This substantially extends v1's cross-judge robustness checks and separate preference study. Existing loss, data, prompt and hyperparameter ablations and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: The five repeated judge runs, means, standard deviations and 95% confidence intervals are unchanged: v1 Tables 14–15 become v3 Tables 13–14. The new human-alignment analysis adds descriptive agreement and calibration metrics, without adding repeated-run information, significance testing or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear in v3 Tables 19–22. For example, Proact-VL with Qwen3-VL scores 59.1 versus the base model's 57.3 on subtitle-free Video-MME, but 52.8 versus 54.5 on LongVideoBench. Human-alignment results report preference agreement and calibration bias. Existing gaming and MVBench results remain unchanged apart from rounding; expanded Table 3 reproduces v1 Appendix Table 10.

T1.justification: The loss formulations, reverse-RoPE derivation in Appendix A.3 and temporal evaluation definitions in Appendix C.1 are retained. The added empirical analyses introduce no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the dataset contribution from constructing the Live Gaming Dataset to explicitly claiming its release. The central claims about proactive streaming interaction, superior response quality and timing, and preservation of general video understanding remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix L newly discusses why LLM judges may underrate LiveStar and overrate Proact-VL, prioritizing preference agreement over absolute-score calibration. Appendix I adds interpretations of Video-MME gains and LongVideoBench regressions as benchmark-specific tradeoffs. The original grounding, frame-rate and entity-recognition limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-homepage link, detailed human annotation instructions in Appendix N.6 and sampling information for the new benchmarks. The loss weights, response-head layer, clipping and evaluation thresholds moved into Section 5.1 were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MVBench, Video-MME, LongVideoBench and VLMEvalKit. The related-work positioning remains essentially unchanged; numerous other reference edits update publication metadata for works already cited.

P1.justification: There are localized contribution-bullet rewrites, wording and heading corrections, and appendix reorganization, including moving Game-Wise Analysis earlier. Implementation paragraphs move into the main text, author information changes, and the final author-contribution statement is removed. Most existing prose and prompt templates remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds four result tables and the human-score comparison plot in Figure 17. It promotes the full common/general results into main Table 3, enlarges the data-pipeline figure and relocates existing displays. These are localized additions and layout changes; the existing illustrations and analytical plots retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added benchmarks strengthen the evidence about retained general video capabilities, while the human-alignment study directly checks scoring reliability and transparently identifies calibration bias. The mixed LongVideoBench results also provide a useful qualification. These improve validation and interpretation, but the gain is incremental because v1 already contains the core experiments, extensive robustness analyses and a human user study.
